definitions.gloss: combustible material; burnable trash; flammable item
definitions.explanation: Materials that can burn. In everyday Japanese life, most commonly refers to burnable garbage in the context of waste sorting.

examples.japanese: {可燃物|かねんぶつ}は{火曜日|かようび}に{出|だ}してください。
examples.english: Please put out burnable trash on Tuesdays.

examples.japanese: ゴミを{可燃物|かねんぶつ}と{不燃物|ふねんぶつ}に{分|わ}けなければならない。
examples.english: You have to separate garbage into burnable and non-burnable items.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}してきたばかりで、{可燃物|かねんぶつ}の{収集日|しゅうしゅうび}がまだわからない。
examples.english: I just moved in and don't know the burnable trash collection day yet.

notes:
USAGE:
Essential vocabulary for daily life in Japan, where garbage separation is strictly enforced. {可燃物|かねんぶつ} (also called {可燃|かねん}ゴミ or {燃|も}えるゴミ) includes paper, food scraps, and some plastics. Each municipality has specific rules.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {可燃物|かねんぶつ}の{日|ひ} (burnable trash day)
- {可燃物|かねんぶつ}{収集|しゅうしゅう} (burnable trash collection)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {不燃物|ふねんぶつ}: non-burnable trash — glass, metals, ceramics
- {燃|も}えるゴミ: burnable garbage — casual, everyday equivalent
- {資源|しげん}ゴミ: recyclable waste — a separate category
